MEDIUMDCS-06.remote_control_apps · Probes for remote-control apps (AnyDesk / TeamViewer)

The app probes URL schemes or bundle IDs of remote-control / remote-support apps (AnyDesk, TeamViewer, QuickSupport), a common anti-fraud SDK pattern.

Vector
DCS-06
Why this severity
Checking for remote-support apps is a fraud signal: WP248 criterion 1 gives screening customers against a fraud database as its example, and criterion 9 covers processing that decides whether a person may use a service.

MEDIUMSECH-01.allows_arbitrary_scoped · ATS relaxed for web, media or local-network content (NSAllowsArbitraryLoadsInWebContent, NSAllowsArbitraryLoadsForMedia)

ATS is relaxed for a class of connections (web content, media, or local-network addresses), permitting cleartext or weak-TLS loads of that traffic. MASTG-TEST-0322 fails on each of these keys.

Vector
SECH-01
Why this severity
Same weakness as the global opt-out, scoped to web content, media or local resources (unqualified and .local names, IP addresses), so less of the app's data is exposed. IP addresses can be anywhere on the internet, so the attack vector stays network.

Remediation (developer): Drop NSAllowsArbitraryLoadsInWebContent, NSAllowsArbitraryLoadsForMedia and NSAllowsLocalNetworking where not needed and load the content over HTTPS. If a specific host needs cleartext, scope it under NSExceptionDomains instead.
For users: On untrusted Wi-Fi, apps with weak transport security can leak data. Avoid sensitive actions on public networks when using such apps.

MEDIUMSECH-01.insecure_exception_domains · ATS exception domains permit cleartext or weak TLS (1)

One or more NSExceptionDomains allow cleartext HTTP loads, a TLS version below 1.2, or connections without forward secrecy. MASTG-TEST-0322 and MASTG-TEST-0342 fail on these settings.

Vector
SECH-01
Why this severity
Per-domain ATS exceptions: the hole is real but bounded to the listed hosts.

INFODCS-01.user_defaults_appgroup_fingerprint · UserDefaults shared within an App Group (declared reason 1C8F.1) reference

A privacy manifest declares required reason 1C8F.1 for the UserDefaults API: the code reads and writes defaults shared with the apps, extensions and App Clips in the same App Group. Apple permits this only within the group and forbids using it for tracking. Inventory: it shows a shared store exists, not what is stored in it. (The rule id is kept for continuity; it used to fire on any UserDefaults declaration and claimed an advertising-ID share nothing in the bundle showed.)

INFODCS-04.face_id_biometrics · FaceID / LocalAuthentication biometrics reference

LocalAuthentication / LAPolicy biometric checks. The app receives only success or failure, never biometric data. Whether the check is event-bound (MASWE-0020) needs the evaluatePolicy call site, which sits in encrypted code, so this records the API for review and is not a weakness on its own.

DCS-04

INFODCS-06.competitor_url_schemes · Checks for specific messenger, social or banking apps

LSApplicationQueriesSchemes names the scheme of a messenger, social or banking app (tg, vk, whatsapp, telegram, instagram, sberbank, alfabank, vtb, tinkoffbank), so -canOpenURL: can tell whether it is installed.

Vector
DCS-06
Why this severity
Which apps are installed says what a person is interested in: WP248 criterion 1 covers profiling from "personal preferences or interests". One criterion is a risk under GDPR, not a likely high risk.

INFODCS-06.ls_application_queries_schemes · Probes installed apps via LSApplicationQueriesSchemes (50 schemes)

The app declares URL schemes it can probe with -canOpenURL:, the iOS analogue of Android's QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES. A short list (deep-linking into a few partner apps) is routine; a long list is an installed-app fingerprinting signal.

INFODCS-07.wifi_info · Wi-Fi network / BSSID inspection

Reads the current Wi-Fi network info (CNCopyCurrentNetworkInfo / NEHotspotHelper / NEHotspotNetwork.fetchCurrent). The BSSID is a stable location proxy, the same access point identifies a physical place across sessions.

Vector
DCS-07
Why this severity
The connected network's BSSID locates the device. Location data: WP248 criterion 4 names it among data of a highly personal nature ("location data whose collection questions the freedom of movement"). One criterion is a risk under GDPR, not a likely high risk.

INFOPLAT-02.custom_url_schemes · Registers 12 custom URL schemes (inbound deep-link surface) reference

The app registers custom URL scheme(s) via CFBundleURLSchemes. Any app or web page can invoke these; if application(_:open:options:) acts on unvalidated parameters, this is an entry point for unauthorized actions. Custom schemes are also unverified (unlike Universal Links). Review the handler for input validation.

INFOSECH-06.dynamic_loader_imports · Dynamic loader in use (dlopen / dlsym) reference

The binary imports dlopen/dlsym, so it can resolve and call code chosen at runtime rather than at link time. That is how optional frameworks, plugin architectures and A/B-tested SDKs are loaded, and it is entirely normal, so this ships as INFO inventory rather than a weakness. It matters only as context: an app that also carries obfuscation (SURV-04) or a data broker (TRK-02) can assemble behaviour a static scan cannot see, and dynamic code loading is the mechanism that makes that possible. Note the limit of the signal: an import proves the symbol is linked, not that it is ever called, and iOS forbids loading code that is not already in the signed bundle. (MASWE-0049)

INFOSURV-01.getifaddrs_import · Imports getifaddrs() for network interface enumeration

Imports the C function getifaddrs() which lists every network interface. NOTE: getifaddrs is also the standard primitive for plain reachability and local-IP discovery and is linked by many networking SDKs, so the import alone is a weak VPN signal that fires on most apps. MASTG / privacy-guide VPN detection keys on NEVPNManager or an explicit tunnel-interface name (utun/ppp/ipsec), kept here as an informational marker only.

INFOSURV-01.utun_interface_string · VPN tunnel interface name in strings

The binary embeds a concrete VPN tunnel interface name like utun0, ipsec0, ppp0 or tap0 (with the trailing digit). Plain "utun" / "ipsec" appear in many legitimate NetworkExtension contexts, so the rule requires the digit suffix that is only meaningful when iterating over real interfaces. Interface names are lowercase, so the match is case-sensitive: "TUN3|" turned up inside compressed data in an ad SDK. "ipsec3" and "ipsec4" are excluded because they are OpenSSL's names for two elliptic curves ("IPSec/IKE/Oakley curve #3/#4"), present in every app that bundles it.

INFOSURV-02.dyld_image_introspection · dyld image-list introspection reference

Calls _dyld_image_count / _dyld_get_image_name, can be used to detect injected dylibs (tweaks, Frida gadget). NOTE: these symbols are also used by crash reporters, analytics SDKs and the Swift runtime to enumerate loaded images, so bare presence is not anti-analysis. OWASP MASTG anti-debugging tests key on ptrace / sysctl(P_TRACED) rather than dyld enumeration, so this is an informational capability marker, not a weakness.

INFOSURV-02.fork_posix_spawn · fork / posix_spawn execution probe mitigation

Calls fork() or posix_spawn(), calling these from a sandboxed iOS app is forbidden; a successful call indicates a jailbroken environment. NOTE: many cross-platform SDKs and the Swift/ObjC runtime merely *link* these symbols without calling them on iOS, so the import alone is a very weak signal and fires on most apps. Treated as informational rather than a weakness (MASTG keys anti-tamper on ptrace / sysctl, not on linked posix symbols).

INFOSURV-02.jailbreak_file_paths · Jailbreak filesystem paths probed mitigation

Hard-codes paths that exist only on jailbroken devices. The narrow primary pattern targets paths that are *only* jailbreak-relevant (Cydia, apt, the MobileSubstrate dylibs and jailbreakd). Broader literals such as `/bin/bash` or `/etc/apt` regularly appear in stock debug strings and are handled by the `ignore-stdlib-debug-paths` suppression; they only re-surface when these higher-signal paths also appear in the same binary.

INFOTRK-04.egress.jp · Endpoints owned by JP-based organisations (1 endpoint)

The bundle references 1 endpoint(s) whose owner is based in JP, owners: LY Corp. The country is the owning organisation's home jurisdiction from the tracker database, not where a server is hosted, and a referenced endpoint is not observed traffic. If the app sends personal data there, it is a third-country transfer: whether that is lawful depends on the safeguards, purpose and paperwork behind it, none of which is visible in a binary. JP holds an EU adequacy decision, so a transfer there needs no additional Chapter V safeguard.

KR holds an EU adequacy decision, so a transfer there needs no additional Chapter V safeguard.

INFOmeta.fairplay_main · Main executable is FairPlay-encrypted reference

The main Mach-O is encrypted by the App Store. Static string scanning of its TEXT segment won't work without a decrypted dump (e.g., via frida-ios-dump or bagbak on a jailbroken device). Embedded frameworks and dylibs are USUALLY ENCRYPTED TOO (measured 91% across the reference corpus; in half of apps every Mach-O is encrypted), so TEXT-segment string recall is limited bundle-wide, not just for the main binary. What still survives encryption is __LINKEDIT: symbols, imported/defined symbol names, ObjC selectors and linked dylibs, which is why symbol-based detection carries this scan rather than string matching.

Vector
SURV-02
Why this severity
Scan metadata: what the scanner could and could not see.
MASVS
MASVS-RESILIENCE
Solove
Surveillance Intrusion
Remediation (developer): For full TEXT-segment coverage, supply a decrypted .ipa produced by frida-ios-dump or bagbak from a jailbroken device. Resource files, plists, entitlements, symbols, selectors and linked dylibs are still scanned in the meantime.
For users: Usually defensive (anti-fraud / anti-tamper). If the app refuses to run on your device for no clear reason, this is often why. No user action needed.
